skill.name: expense-update
skill.description: Update, recategorize, or delete expense records.

attachment.anyPhrases: recategorize,change category,set category,fix category,reclassify,wrong category,should be,correct category,delete expense,remove expense,edit expense,update expense,is clothes,is food,is shop,is coffee,categorize,clothes category,food category

skill.update_intent:
0. If `expense-ledger-schema` is not already in the prompt or tool history, call `read_skill("expense-ledger-schema")` in the same turn as any independent lookups below (do not wait for a separate turn). 1. `get_categories()` if needed — resolve category name to numeric `public.category.id`. 2. Narrow `SELECT id, name, amount, paid_date, category FROM public.expense ...` to find target row IDs. Never update by merchant name alone. 3. Scoped `UPDATE public.expense SET category = <id> WHERE id IN (...)` or `DELETE FROM public.expense WHERE id IN (...)` — PK only. 4. Verify with a follow-up `SELECT` on the same IDs before confirming to the user.
After an UPDATE or DELETE, verify with exactly this query (replace IDs):
```sql SELECT e.id, e.name, e.amount, e.paid_date, e.category, c.name AS category_name FROM public.expense AS e LEFT JOIN public.category AS c ON e.category = c.id WHERE e.id IN (...); ```
Whenever a query joins tables, qualify every selected column with its table alias (e.g. `e.id`, `c.name`). Never use bare `id`, `name`, or `category` in a join.
For conversational corrections (e.g. "UNIQLO is Clothes"): - Infer merchant from context and category from the user's statement. - If multiple rows match, update all shown in recent context or ask which dates to change.
